summary: Evren is a blink comparator for NASA's SPHEREx space telescope. In 1930 Clyde Tombaugh found Pluto by flipping between two photographs of the same stars. Evren does the same with SPHEREx: it finds every SPHEREx image of a patch of sky, aligns them, subtracts the sky that never changes, links whatever moved, and checks each mover against every known asteroid and comet. On its own, Evren found Pluto in 6 separate SPHEREx visits and recovered known asteroids exactly where their orbits put them, across 236 frames in 5 fields. Evren also measured Pluto's infrared spectrum from 72 SPHEREx exposures and found the fingerprint of methane ice: at 3.3 microns Pluto reflects only about 4 percent of the light it reflects near 1 micron.
details: Evren is a public web tool that shows how the sky changes in NASA SPHEREx images, the way Clyde Tombaugh's blink comparator did in 1930. Pick a field and Evren finds every SPHEREx Level 2 image that covers it, reads only the pixels it needs, and puts every frame on one north up grid using each image's own sky coordinates. It builds a median static sky, subtracts it, and finds what changed above the noise. Spots that line up in several exposures of one visit become tracklets, while one time hits like cosmic rays drop out. Every tracklet is compared with IMCCE SkyBoT predictions for that exact moment, so known asteroids and comets are labeled and anything unmatched becomes a candidate. The viewer lets anyone flip between two dates, step through a year of frames, see the changes view and the static sky, and click each find. Results: Pluto found in 6 separate SPHEREx visits, and known asteroids recovered exactly where their orbits put them, across 236 frames in 5 fields. Evren also uses SPHEREx's 102 colors: each exposure that catches Pluto measures one point of its spectrum, and 72 exposures show the deep methane ice band at 3.3 microns. Built with Python (NumPy, SciPy, Astropy, Pillow) and plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages. Code: https://github.com/onatcakici/evren
dataRefs: NASA SPHEREx Level 2 spectral images (NASA IPAC Infared Science Archive)
projectRefs: IMCCE SkyBoT, known asteroids and comets
